item.title: Russia chose 'Easter escalation' over ceasefire, says Zelensky
item.summary: Six civilians were killed and 40 others injured as Russia launched hundreds of drones and missiles.

item.title: French-owned ship passes through Strait of Hormuz
item.summary: It appears to be the first ship owned by a major European firm to go through the strait since the conflict began.

item.title: Burkina Faso must 'forget' about democracy, military leader says
item.summary: Capt Ibrahim Traoré, who seized power in 2023, says democratic rule would not work for his country.

item.title: Faced with new energy shock, Europe asks if reviving nuclear is the answer
item.summary: As war drives up gas and fuel prices, Europeans turn again to the issue of energy independence.

item.title: Football rally in Peru leaves one dead and dozens injured
item.summary: Hundreds of Alianza Lima fans had gathered for a pregame rally ahead of a match against local rivals Universitario de Deportes.

item.title: Judge dismisses most of Blake Lively's claims in Justin Baldoni harassment suit
item.summary: The judge left in place three allegations against Baldoni, meaning the civil trial will go ahead next month.

item.title: Rescue team in Iran face 'harrowing and dangerous' search for US crew member
item.summary: A former US marine tells the BBC the priority of any recovery team would be to look for signs of life.

item.title: Artemis II crew now halfway to Moon as they take 'spectacular' image of Earth
item.summary: The snap was taken aboard the Orion capsule by its commander, Reid Wiseman, as the crew head towards the Moon.

item.title: Italy's Uffizi Galleries targeted in cyber-attack but deny security breach
item.summary: Hackers were reported to have infiltrated IT systems - but the gallery says its works are safe.

item.title: France's Muslim gathering ban overturned by courts
item.summary: The Paris police department had argued that the four-day gathering was a security threat because it could be a target of terrorism.
